From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & safety evals — next steps

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: evaluate model fit for clinical summarization and triage suggestions, with strong refusal/safety behavior for PHI and medical advice.
- Primary constraints: no long-term retention of PHI in logs, redaction for PII in transcripts, and strict refusal patterns for diagnostics/medication recommendations.
- What you offered: a sample eval set (de-identified + a small PHI-conditioned subset), current prompt sets, and your success criteria (precision of suggestions, safety/refusal rates).

Next steps I propose: 
1) You share the drive folder with the eval prompts and sample conversations (we can accept de-identified CSV + a small PHI-tagged sample under NDA).
2) We run an initial model-fit sweep (3 models / 2 quantization profiles) and return a short benchmark: quality metrics, latency, token cost, and safety/regression flags.
3) If results look good, agree on a 2-week pilot on Dedicated sandbox for end-to-end throughput and RLHF/safety probe runs.

I've attached a short mutual action plan and timeline for review (mutual_action_plan.pdf).

Questions for you now: 1) Are there any model families you prefer us not to evaluate for compliance reasons? 2) Any additional redline terms for refusal wording (e.g., must include explicit escalation steps)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — this aligns with what Alex and I discussed internally. A few quick notes: 

- We will not allow any model families that have known licensing restrictions that prevent on-prem deployment; prefer permissive/open families or Redwood-verified variants.
- For refusal wording: we need the model to avoid giving prescriptive medical advice (no dosing, no diagnosis). If a model suggests next steps it should always include a clinician escalation sentence and cite uncertainty.

I've shared the folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-HealthScopeEval (permission granted to marissa@redwoodinference.com). The folder includes: medical_prompts.csv (sample prompts + expected redaction flags), a small PHI-tagged set (PHI_SAMPLE_01.csv) under NDA, and a short doc with success criteria.

Attaching medical_prompts.csv for quick reference. Please let me know if you need a separate upload method.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood can run the initial safety/refusal probes without persisting any PHI outside the sandbox? That's a hard requirement for us.

Speak soon,
Priya Menon

Priya —

Appreciate the shared folder and the clear constraints. Quick answers and our plan (high level):

- PHI handling: We can run initial probes in a Dedicated sandbox that does not persist logs to the control plane (we will redact or hash identifiers before any long-term storage). Rishi, can you confirm the exact retention policy we will use for the sandbox run?

- Model recommendations for the first sweep:
  1) redwood-llama-65b-v2 (float16) — baseline for language capability and instruction-following
  2) redwood-rlhf-safety-13b (safety-tuned) — to test refusal behavior and guardrail adherence
  3) open-compat-7b-quant (int4) — cost-efficient baseline to check tradeoffs

We will run the following evaluations: quality (ROUGE/BERTScore), hallucination/responsiveness checks, safety/refusal probes (custom prompt set you provided + additional adversarial prompts), latency and token cost. Expected deliverable: a short report + sample outputs + a flagged list of any quality regressions vs. your success criteria.

Proposed timeline:
- 1-2 business days: confirm access and test job (sanity run on 50 prompts)
- 3-5 business days: full model sweep on de-identified set (scale as needed)
- 1-2 business days: safety probe runs including PHI-conditioned cases (in sandbox)

Next steps:
1) Rishi and I will coordinate the technical plan and share a proposed eval spreadsheet (proposed_eval_plan.xlsx).
2) Priya — confirm that the PHI_SAMPLE_01.csv is covered under the NDA and that the limited access terms are acceptable (we will not persist PHI outside sandbox).

Hi Priya / Marissa —

Quick technical note from the evaluation side:

- Retention/Logging: For the Dedicated sandbox run we will enable ephemeral job logs that are encrypted and destroyed after 24 hours. No plaintext PHI will be persisted to the control plane. We will also apply token-level redaction for any PII fields you flagged in PHI_SAMPLE_01.csv; the redaction transform will be applied prior to any model input storage.

- Safety probes: We'll run three classes of guardrail prompts: refusal triggers (explicit requests for prescriptions/diagnoses), red-team adversarial prompts (indirect pressure tests), and policy-compliance prompts (asking for escalation language). We'll log model responses and a safety score per prompt; any response that violates the refusal policy will be flagged for immediate review.

- Deliverables:
  * CSV of inputs + model outputs (redacted where necessary)
  * Safety flags + severity level
  * Short runbook describing how to interpret refusal behaviors and recommended mitigations (temperature, prompt templates, and a fallback policy).

We can start the 50-prompt sanity run as soon as we receive confirmation that PHI_SAMPLE_01.csv access under the NDA is permitted. Priya — please confirm and let us know if you want us to run on Hosted (with encrypted logs) vs. Dedicated sandbox. Given your requirement to avoid persistence, Dedicated sandbox is recommended.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-minute tech sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com
